newsitem.title: USA: Mobil begins new production off Alabama.
newsitem.headline: Mobil begins new production off Alabama.

text.p: Mobil Corp said it has begun producing natural gas from its Mobile 869 field in federal waters off the shore of Alabama.

The addition of production from the Mobile 869 field to Mobil's existing operations in its Lower Mobile Bay - Mary Ann and Mobile 823 fields - increases Mobil-operated gas production from offshore Alabama wells to more than 400 million cubic feet per day from about 320 million cubic feet daily, with Mobil net working interest production increasing to about 250 million cubic feet per day from 210 million cubic feet daily.

Drilled to a measured depth of 22,090 feet four miles south of Dauphin Island, the Mobile 869-3 well tested natural gas at a rate of 84 million cubic feet a day with a flowing tubing pressure of 4,235 pounds per square inch.
Mobil has a 49-percent interest in the Mobile 869 Field.
Partners are Exxon Corp and Texaco Inc with 30 percent and 21 percent interests, respectively.

"The development of the Mobile 869 field adds profitable production for Mobil in the U.S., and is another indication of the increasing importance and potential of Alabama's prolific Norphlet (natural) gas play," said Mobil Exploration & Producing U.S. Inc President Mike Yeager.
"The excellent flow rate and gas quality from this field demonstrate the continuing attractiveness of the Mobile Bay trend."
Mobil said it expects a further increase in its offshore Alabama natural gas production around mid-year with the streaming of the Aloe Bay Field in state waters north of Dauphin Island.
